description: The Open DS grammar: a finite set of questions a design system must answer. Reasons come first (business, people, content, tasks, human factors, outcomes, brand, use scenarios, team). Scopes follow, from typography to voice and tone. Every scope answers the same five method questions (roles, how many, how defined, values, lands in) and has the same parts: the tokens it owns, the components it lands in and its situations. Each scheme answers every question, and each answer says why and which earlier answers it follows from. Situations are the moments where people need to know what to use; each scheme answers them too. Component keys are the shared component API every scheme fills.

ai.use_when: You need the list of questions behind a design system, or the meaning of a question id such as typography.definition or a situation id such as number-in-table.
ai.how_to_read: Reasons are answered first. A scope answer lists in 'because' the answers that pulled it. Scope question ids are <scope>.<method>, so typography.values and voice.values answer the same kind of question. Tokens follow from the answers. Components read only component keys. Written text in a scheme (voice, scenarios) lists in 'follows' the answers it was written from.

layers.description: Why the system exists: product, people, content, tasks, human factors, outcomes, brand, use scenarios, team.
The design decisions: typography, color, spacing, shape, elevation, motion, iconography, theming, accessibility, naming, voice and tone, components. Each answers the five method questions.
Primitives are the options. Semantics are the decisions, in light and dark. Brands and modes are themes.
One key per component element, variant and state. Every scheme fills every key.

methods.title: Roles
methods.description: Which roles the scope needs. Each role becomes a group of decisions.

methods.title: How many
methods.description: How many steps, levels or variants each role gets.

methods.title: How defined
methods.description: The rule that produces the values: a scale, a base unit, a style or a policy.

methods.title: Values
methods.description: Where the values sit, as a word. The exact values live in the tokens.

methods.title: Lands in
methods.description: Where the scope does its most visible work in the product.

reasons.title: Business and product
reasons.description: Why the product exists and what it does for the business. It frames every later answer.

questions.text: What does the product do for the business?
questions.description: The main job of the product. Operating tools, publishing, selling and public services pull the system in different directions.

questions.text: How many brands or products share the system?
questions.description: One brand keeps the system small. Many brands need a theming layer.

reasons.title: People and work context
reasons.description: Who uses the product, how often and with what abilities.

questions.description: The main audience. Experts learn an interface; occasional visitors must understand it at first sight.

questions.text: What accessibility level do we commit to?
questions.description: The accessibility promise. It sets floors for contrast, targets and states.

options.label: AA, with AAA where it is cheap

questions.description: Numbers, long text, forms and media each need different type, spacing and color.

questions.text: How much is on one screen?
questions.description: Information density. It drives spacing, type size and how groups separate.

reasons.title: Tasks and flows
reasons.description: What people do with the content.

questions.description: The task that must be fastest. Comparing, reading, completing and exploring need different layouts.

questions.text: How often do people repeat actions?
questions.description: Repetition. Frequent actions must be quiet and fast; rare ones can be explicit.
The scarce human resource on this product.

questions.text: How do people recall the interface?
questions.description: Learned interfaces can rely on recognition. Fresh visits need explicit labels.

options.label: They learn it and recognise it
They see it fresh each time

reasons.title: Outcomes
reasons.description: What success looks like and what failure costs.

questions.description: The measure the system optimises for.
The error the system must make hard.

reasons.title: Brand
reasons.description: How the brand should feel in the interface.

questions.text: What should the brand feel like?
questions.description: The feeling the interface carries.

questions.text: How visible is the brand in the interface?
questions.description: How much brand expression the product carries.

reasons.title: Use scenarios
reasons.description: Where and for how long people use the product. Written scenarios follow from these answers.

questions.description: The place and device. A desk with a mouse, a phone on the move, or anything at all.
Session length. All-day use rewards learning; short visits must work at first sight.

reasons.title: Team and delivery
reasons.description: Who keeps the system right, and how fast it changes.

questions.description: Team size limits how many tokens and variants can stay correct.
Change rate. Fast change needs a stable component API and a flexible theme.

scopes.title: Typography
scopes.description: How text is set: roles, sizes and line height.

questions.text: Which text roles does it need?
questions.description: The set of text roles. Each role becomes a type decision.

questions.text: How many steps does the type scale take?
questions.description: Few sizes keep a dense screen calm. More sizes give long pages a clear hierarchy.

options.label: Only the steps the screens need
options.description: The scale keeps the few sizes the screens use, and nothing in between.

options.label: One step per kind of text
options.description: One size each for caption, body, heading, title and display.

options.label: Fine steps, so pages can set their own rhythm
options.description: Many close sizes, so a page can tune its hierarchy and pace.

questions.text: How are sizes and line heights defined?
questions.description: A ratio scale with line heights on the grid, a ratio scale with proportional line heights, or fixed steps.

options.label: A ratio, line heights on the grid
A ratio, line heights in proportion

questions.description: Body size relative to the usual default.

questions.text: Where does type do the most work?
questions.description: The place where type decisions matter most.

scopes.title: Color
scopes.description: How color carries action, state and brand.

questions.text: Which color roles does it need?
questions.description: The groups of color decisions.

questions.text: How many emphasis levels do actions need?
questions.description: The number of action styles, from primary to quiet.
Neutrals and one brand ramp, or a shared base with a ramp per brand.

options.label: Shared neutrals, a ramp per brand

questions.description: Overall color intensity.

questions.text: Where does color carry meaning first?
questions.description: The place where color does its most important job.

scopes.title: Spacing
scopes.description: How space shows what belongs together.

questions.text: Which spacing roles does it need?
questions.description: The groups of space decisions.
One density for everything, or a second for dense views.
A fine base unit gives small steps for dense screens; a coarse one gives big, even steps.
The base density.
The place where space does its most visible work.

questions.text: Which shape roles does it need?
questions.description: The elements that get their own corner.
How many different corners appear.
One fixed set for the product, or a set per brand.
The corner of buttons and inputs.
The place where corners are seen most.

scopes.title: Elevation
scopes.description: When something rises above the page, and what separates groups.

questions.description: The layers that get a shadow.
The number of distinct shadows.

questions.text: What separates groups on the page?
questions.description: The device that tells the eye a new group starts.
Shadow character.
The place where layering is seen.

scopes.title: Motion
scopes.description: What moves, why and how fast.

questions.description: The jobs motion does.
The number of distinct durations.
A standard ease-out, or a spring that overshoots.
Speed as a word. The convention behind each word is in the primitives.
The place where motion is seen.

scopes.title: Iconography
scopes.description: When icons appear and how they look.

questions.description: The jobs icons carry.
The number of icon sizes.
Stroke or fill.

questions.text: How big are icons next to text?
questions.description: Icon size relative to text.
The place where icons are seen most.
The axes a theme varies along.
Brands times modes.
Single brand, or brands as theme modes over shared semantics.
The modes the semantic layer carries. Light and dark are standard.

questions.text: What changes when the theme changes?
questions.description: The decisions a theme switch touches.

questions.text: Which states get their own visible value?
questions.description: States with a distinct look.

questions.text: How many signals carry each meaning?
questions.description: Whether status relies on color alone or also on icons and words.

questions.text: What contrast floor do we hold?
questions.description: Contrast commitment for text.
The smallest clickable size.

questions.text: Where are the floors hardest to hold?
questions.description: The place where accessibility needs the most care.

scopes.title: Naming
scopes.description: How tokens and keys are named.

questions.description: Tokens only, or tokens and a component API.
Primitives and semantics, or also component keys.
Role names survive change; component names are local.
The spelling of every name.
A component API: one key per element, variant and state.

scopes.title: Voice and tone
scopes.description: How the product speaks: the words in every component.

questions.text: Which kinds of copy does it need?
questions.description: The groups of words the product writes.

questions.text: How many tones does it use?
questions.description: One tone everywhere, a tone per moment, or a shared core with a tone per brand.
The rule that keeps copy consistent.

options.label: A shared core, brand tone on top

questions.description: The voice as a word.

questions.text: Where do the words matter most?
questions.description: The place where copy does its most important job.

scopes.title: Components
scopes.description: Which components the system carries: its inventory, picked from the catalogue.

questions.text: Which component families does it need?
questions.description: The families of the catalogue the inventory draws from. Core is action, form, feedback, overlay, layout and navigation.

options.label: Actions, forms, feedback, overlays, layout and navigation

questions.text: How far does the inventory reach?
questions.description: The size of the inventory, as a word. The inventory follows the needs; the word describes it and sets no limit.

options.label: Only what today's screens use
options.description: A component joins when a screen in use needs it, not before.

options.label: What today's screens use, plus what the next ones will likely need
options.description: Covers the screens in use and the ones the team can see coming, so they find the parts ready.

options.label: Everything its families offer, ready before it's asked for
options.description: Every component the admitted families hold is there from the start, so teams never wait for one.

questions.text: How does a component earn its place?
questions.description: The rule that admits a component into the inventory.

options.label: Its family is in the roles, so product teams find it ready
It works for everyone, with any device and assistive technology
It gives the brand a moment

questions.text: When does a component get another look?
questions.description: Variants and sizes per component, as a word.

options.label: Only when the meaning changes
options.description: A new variant only for a different meaning, such as the main action or a danger.

options.label: Also for emphasis and size
options.description: Variants also set how loud a component is and how much room it takes.

options.label: Also so each brand or page can look its own way
options.description: Variants also let a brand or a page carry its own look on the same component.

questions.text: Where do components do the most work?
questions.description: The screens where the inventory is used most.

components.description: Triggers an action. Variants: primary, secondary, ghost.
Single-line text entry, also used by select.

catalogue.description: Every component a design system can carry: the UI components of the shadcn/ui registry (style new-york-v4, MIT), plus toast, which Open DS builds itself, data-table, which wraps TanStack Table after shadcn's Data Table guide, and date-picker, after shadcn's Date Picker. Each scheme picks its inventory from this list through the components scope. The component-api keys in components cover the ones built so far.
